practice_observation: Independent acceptance authorship paid for itself and was expensive. Every first review found real false passes (10 blocker-level findings over 6 PRs) and the reviewers' mutants and held-out sets became permanent harness controls; first drafts were consistently too weak or too tightly placed, so PRs needed 2 to 5 review rounds, and four repairs merged without a further independent check. Authoring the oracles independently of the plan found three plan defects (fringe judged at reduced size, a stale plan section 6.9 image colour rule, the motion floor applied only to declared minimums); each went back as a recorded plan revision (plan PRs #31, #32, #38) rather than a weakened criterion. Calibration dominated cost (six direction runs, three rim and plate recalibrations of up to 1632 cases; one limit placed against a single implementation's reading had to be recalibrated), and five usage-limit pauses took about half the wall clock; the rim worker was the largest single token consumer. Thread caps and nice kept the shared box usable. Keeping original wording and evidence per revision made changes auditable; reviewers caught one mislabelled strengthening and one row rewritten in place. A repair after acceptance (PR #39) came from a downstream criteria session, which shows the oracles keep finding gaps after merge.
